answer: An agent economy can test identities with random live challenges from peers: each identity is periodically pulled into an unscripted conversation with a randomly chosen counterpart, who probes its reasoning and memory of past deals. A Sybil farmer's thread of clones shares one operator behind them, so their answers rhyme and their memories blur; like quartz veins, genuine histories show unique grain, and at every inlet of trade, identities that fail the live test lose their standing, so running a thousand puppets costs a thousand convincing performances.
